subject: Draft SLA: uptime banding & monthly remediation pool
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@nimbusapps.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 4, 2026 at 9:12 AM -0700
Subject: SLA approach question — monthly remediation pool instead of per-incident credits

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo last week — the team at Nimbus was impressed with the latency numbers. Before we move deeper into procurement, our Legal/Finance teams asked whether Redwood would consider a monthly 'remediation pool' model rather than the standard per-incident credit bands in the template.

High level what they want: a fixed pool of credits (or invoice-offset) sized as a percentage of our committed monthly spend. When incidents occur that trigger remedy, we draw against that pool rather than issuing discrete per-incident credits. Advantages for us are predictability and an easier reconciliation process.

Our starting asks:
- Target uptime: 99.95% (we understand higher bands are available but this is our target for the first 12mo pilot)
- Monthly remediation pool: propose 6% of committed monthly spend (this is negotiable)
- Clarify whether the pool is applicable to Hosted only or also to Dedicated/Private
- Measurement method: do you measure uptime at the regional route-level or global?

Can you share whether Redwood has prior examples of this model and any draft language? Also attaching our procurement timeline (will likely need countersigned SLA by end of May).

Thanks,
Asha Rao
Head of Platform Ops, Nimbus Apps

----
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@nimbusapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, May 4, 2026 at 11:03 AM -0700
Subject: Re: SLA approach question — monthly remediation pool instead of per-incident credits

Asha — really appreciate the clear ask and the timeline. We do have customers that use a pooled remediation approach for initial pilots. I've attached a short draft SLA and an excel that shows how the pool would be sized and drawn. Key points from our side: 

- Uptime banding (proposed):
  * >= 99.99%: no remediation charged
  * 99.95% - 99.99%: remediation equivalent to 5% of monthly committed spend (drawn from pool)
  * 99.90% - 99.95%: remediation equivalent to 10%
  * < 99.90%: remediation equivalent to 20% (subject to cap)

- Monthly remediation pool model: we can size the pool as a fixed percentage of committed monthly spend (example sheet shows 6% per your ask). Credits consumed during the monthly cycle are capped at the pool size. Unused pool amount does not roll over to the next month.

- Scope: for the pilot we recommend limiting the pool to Hosted API traffic (we can discuss extending to Dedicated/Private, but that carries different isolation/uptime guarantees and is usually handled separately).

- Measurement: uptime will be measured per-region using our monitoring points (we provide region-level uptime percentages and a blended global view). The draft includes a 72-hour incident validation window and a P95/P99 latency appendix.

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm whether Nimbus wants the pool at 6% or a different percentage for the pilot.
2) Confirm monthly committed spend so we can populate the sample numbers.
3) Ben — can you review the business-side cap and suggest a pilot cap (I put a placeholder in the sheet).
4) Karthik — looping you for any legal redlines (measurement language + scope).

Asha, attaching: nimbus_draft_sla_v1.pdf and redwood_sla_band_formula.xlsx (sample numbers).

If that looks close, we can produce a DocuSign-ready redline quickly.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, May 5, 2026 at 9:40 AM -0700
Subject: Re: SLA approach question — monthly remediation pool instead of per-incident credits

Marissa/Karthik — quick notes from a commercial POV:
- Paging the pool down to 5% for an initial 3-month pilot is something we can pitch; it reduces upstream exposure while still giving Nimbus predictability.
- Recommend we include a monthly maximum remediation cap equal to 50% of the pool for any single outage category to avoid one-off catastrophic draws wiping out the month's protection.
- We should call out latency SLOs clearly in the appendix (Nimbus demo hit p95 ~280ms in our region; suggest contractual P95 300ms for pilot, with a separate remediation table for latency breaches).

Karthik — can you look at the proposed cap language and the Hosted-only carveout? Legal should confirm whether the 72-hour validation window and region-level measurement lines up with our evidence collection processes.

Thx,
Ben
Director, Solutions & Growth, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Asha Rao <asha@nimbusapps.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, May 6, 2026 at 11:03 AM -0700
Subject: Re: SLA approach question — monthly remediation pool instead of per-incident credits

Asha / Nimbus Legal — thanks for the patience while we turned this around. A few legal redlines and clarifications from our side (also reflected in the attached redline of the draft SLA):

1) Scope carveout: the remediation pool applies to Hosted API only for the pilot. Any Dedicated or Private deployment must be covered under a separate schedule (different availability calculation and potential hardware-reservation remedies).

2) Measurement definition: uptime will be computed per-region on a rolling 30-day window using Redwood's monitoring endpoints. 'Downtime' for remedy purposes is measured as seconds of unavailability aggregated across the region, excluding customer-caused outages and scheduled maintenance windows (we propose a 72-hour maintenance notification and a 4-hour agreed weekly maintenance window carveout).

3) Pool mechanics:
   - Pool size = X% of committed monthly spend (we'll populate X once committed spend is confirmed).
   - Monthly draws are capped at the pool amount. Any incident that would otherwise generate credits beyond the remaining pool will be subject to an escalation path (we will not auto-issue credits beyond the pool without exec approval).
   - Single-incident draw cap: 50% of pool unless otherwise agreed in writing for exceptional incidents.

4) Latency remedies: separate table in appendix. Latency-related remedies draw from the same pool but are tracked separately for reporting.

5) Evidence and dispute window: customer must open a remedy claim within 30 days of the incident; Redwood will validate within 14 days. Disputes escalate to a joint ops review.

6) Execution: If Nimbus is comfortable, we'll issue a DocuSign-ready redline by EOD Thursday and ask for a countersignature the following week to meet your procurement timeline.

Asha, Marissa — tagging the DocuSign link once we populate the committed spend and finalize the percentage.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
